title: GPU pool space & surge scenarios — thermal risk register and runbook
content:
Purpose:
This working workbook defines plausible surge scenarios for on-prem and colocation GPU pools, captures thermal and power risk items, and provides a short runbook for rapid mitigation during high-utilization events. The aim is pragmatic: give SRE/ops and deployment engineering a checklist + estimated actions for the next 90 days while we finalize placement automation.

Scope:
- Applies to datahall racks hosting Redwood Dedicated and Private customer GPU pools in NA-EAST-1 and EU-WEST-2 colos.
- Focus: rack power budget, per-rack cooling headroom (CRAC impact), physical slot allocation and safe surge operating points.
- Excludes: network bandwidth design and on-board firmware upgrades (separate tracks).

Assumptions & constants used in quick calcs:
- Reference GPU name: A100-80GB equiv; nominal draw under typical steady inferencing: 350W per card.
- Typical rack: 8x GPU nodes, each node 4 GPUs = 32 GPUs/rack.
- Base IT load (non-GPU) per rack: 1200W.
- PDU available capacity: 25kW per rack (configured), CRAC chilled-water capacity per aisle: rated 150kW.
- Safety headroom target: 15% of PDU capacity reserved for transient spikes and management/PSUs.

Baseline calculations (per rack):
- GPU steady power: 32 gpus * 350W = 11,200W
- Total steady rack IT load = 11,200W + 1,200W = 12,400W (~12.4kW)
- Headroom vs PDU: 25kW - 12.4kW = 12.6kW (50% headroom)
- With 15% safety reserve: usable = 25kW * 0.85 = 21.25kW -> surge room = 21.25kW - 12.4kW = 8.85kW
- Equivalent additional GPU capacity (peak) = 8,850W / 350W ≈ 25 GPUs burstable for short durations.

Surge scenarios (probabilities are qualitative):
1) Short burst (30-90s) — model warmup or bulk-batched backfill (likelihood: high):
   - Typical pattern: whole-pod KV cache warming leads to synchronized token bursts; rack-level power can spike 20–40%.
   - Impact: if sustained >90s, PDU alarms may trigger. Thermal delta: +4–8°C at outlet if airflow stable.
   - Mitigation: enable transient autoshed on low-priority requests; shift traffic to neighbor racks via smart routing; enable KV-caching to reduce re-gen where possible.

2) Sustained high utilization (10–30 minutes) — scheduled load or runaway job (likelihood: medium):
   - Sustained additional draw 30% -> rack becomes 16.12kW -> with reserve still OK, but CRAC load + aisle temp creep.
   - Impact: adjacent racks see +2–3°C; if aisle CRAC already at 80% baseline, risk of temp alarm within 20 min.
   - Mitigation: trigger canary fallbacks to lower-power model quantization profile; actively migrate jobs to other colo region if available; call colo facilities to temporarily boost chilled water flow (if SOP allows).

3) Partial PDU failure / breaker trip (likelihood: low):
   - Effect: effective PDU capacity reduced to ~12.5kW; with base load ~12.4kW we are at risk immediately.
   - Mitigation: graceful draining of non-critical instances, emergency migration of reserved customers to cloud/dedicated, manual power redistribution (per PDU layout).

4) Aisle CRAC degradation (likelihood: low-medium):
   - One CRAC falls offline, aisle capacity drops from 150kW -> 100kW net; if multiple racks already near 60% utilization, temperature will climb across the aisle.
   - Mitigation: proactive load shedding across racks in affected aisle; enable spreading policy for new inflight sessions; contact colo ops and shift redundant workloads to hot-standby regions.

Thermal & risk register (short form) — risk id, trigger, immediate action, owner, RTO
- R1: Rack PDU overload -> breaker alarm trips -> immediate: throttle GPU clocks (if supported) + de-schedule best-effort pools -> owner: Marcus Valdez -> RTO: 5m
- R2: Aisle temp exceeds 30C -> temp alarm on CRAC -> immediate: throttle batch traffic, enable cooling priority, notify colo -> owner: Priya Nair -> RTO: 15m
- R3: Persistent >20% utilization for >15m -> sustained thermal creep -> immediate: migrate critical live sessions to alternate pools, apply quantized models -> owner: Avery Chen -> RTO: 30m
- R4: Cooling water supply lag during maintenance window -> ambient rise across multiple aisles -> immediate: deny new deployments in affected racks, enable rapid failover -> owner: Elena Ortiz -> RTO: 1h

Short-run mitigation recipes (runbook steps, 0–60 minutes):
0) Detection: dashboard alert (per-rack power >80% or aisle temp >28C) -> page on-call SRE.
1) 0–2m: Confirm telemetry (PDU, inlet/outlet temps, rack door sensor, CRAC status). Post initial incident note: incident-channel '#ops/colo-incidents' and tag INFRA-1832.
2) 2–5m: Immediate soft-mitigation: set routing policy to spill low-priority queues to cloud-hosted inference. Activate model quantization profile on impacted model routes (RoutePolicy: quantize-high->quantize-mid).
3) 5–15m: If condition persists, start rolling graceful drain of best-effort tenant pools on impacted rack(s). Notify customers with expected degraded performance for up to 60 minutes.
4) 15–60m: If thermal trend continues upward or PDU trips occur, escalate: execute cross-rack migration plan (documented in linked Confluence), coordinate with colo to increase CRAC cooling or perform breaker inspection.

Operational notes & engineering actions to close gaps (next 90 days):
- Instrument per-node inlet thermistors and correlate with token latency spikes; add heatmap to console per-route. Owner: Samir Haddad.
- Add an automated transient-shed policy to the serving runtime that kicks in at per-node power >420W/GPU for >45s. Owner: Avery Chen.
- Revise rack slotting plan to avoid mixing two high-power customers in the same PDU quadrants; target by 2026-06. Owner: Priya Nair.
- Run a single-aisle failover DR drill (simulate one CRAC offline) and verify migration paths. Owner: Elena Ortiz.

Quick reference checklists (for on-call):
- Before paging colo: verify metrics and take screenshots, confirm whether adjacent racks show similar trends.
- If breaker alarm: run PDU layout map, identify redundant circuit, prepare to migrate nodes.
- For thermal alarm: apply quantized model profiles, reduce batching, and re-route low-priority traffic.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Define acceptable customer SLA for emergency migration windows (ask product/legal to confirm contractual allowances).
- Evaluate feasibility of localized liquid cooling for top-end racks (cost/benefit).
- Decide whether to pre-provision a small burst-capacity pool in a different colo for immediate failover (cost impact analysis needed).

Appendix: quick numeric examples used during ops
- 1 extra GPU-equivalent sustained = 350W -> 2.857kW buys ~8 extra GPUs.
- To maintain 15% safety reserve on 25kW PDU, sustained load must stay below 21.25kW.

End of working workbook — comments welcome. This doc is intentionally operational and terse; will be iterated after the DR drill on 2026-05-10.
